cards.title: OUTLINE FOR RADIO REPORT
pearls: Lead with agency, unit, destination and level of care; give patient age, sex, consciousness and chief complaint.
Include vital signs, pertinent exam and history, interventions, response, destination and ETA. Report stroke findings and last known well when relevant.

cards.title: GENERAL PATIENT ASSESSMENT
pearls: Scene safety and PPE first; assess airway, breathing, circulation, neurologic status and exposure.
Record SAMPLE, initial vital signs, pain score and GCS; reassess ABCDs.

cards.title: CONSIDERATIONS FOR PATIENTS WITH SPECIAL HEALTHCARE NEEDS
pearls: Ask caregivers about the patient’s baseline and consult any emergency care plan.
Assess the patient systematically even when a chronic condition or disability changes the usual presentation.

cards.title: STREAMLINED COMMUNICATION
pearls: Streamlined communication applies to qualifying BLS calls only. Confirm inclusion and exclusion criteria with your system before using it.
Transmit the core patient presentation and destination information required by the system’s process.

cards.title: INITIATION OF ALS CARE
pearls: Adult guideline triggers include pulse below 60 or above 130, respiratory rate below 10 or above 30, systolic pressure below 90 or above 200, or irregularity.
Potentially life-threatening conditions can trigger ALS regardless of vital signs; downgrading requires online Medical Direction.

cards.title: LOAD-AND-GO SITUATIONS
pearls: Package and limit scene time when hospital care is needed for stability. Document the condition and any omitted or abbreviated procedure.
Load and go does not itself mean faster driving.

cards.title: WITHHOLDING OR WITHDRAWING OF RESUSCITATIVE EFFORTS
pearls: If unsure whether a withholding policy applies, begin treatment and contact Medical Direction.
A living will or a surrogate does not directly authorize EMS to withhold resuscitation under this order; verify a written POLST/DNR under system policy.

cards.title: DEFIBRILLATION AND CARDIOVERSION ENERGY DOSING GUIDE
pearls: Use the dosing table for the patient’s age, rhythm, and device. Check the defibrillation and cardioversion energy separately.
This is primarily an ALS reference; an EMT should recognize when to support CPR/AED operation and request ALS.

cards.title: EMERGING INFECTIOUS DISEASE GUIDANCE
pearls: Screen symptoms and exposure history according to the disease guidance and use appropriate PPE.
The source contains a flowchart; check current agency and public-health guidance for the pathogen-specific pathway.

cards.title: ADULT GLASGOW COMA SCALE (GCS)
pearls: Adult GCS totals eye, verbal, and motor response. Record the components as well as the total, and trend changes.

cards.title: PEDIATRIC GLASGOW COMA SCALE (PGCS)
pearls: Use the age-appropriate pediatric verbal and motor responses; trend the component scores and total.

cards.title: AIRWAY OBSTRUCTION
pearls: For a conscious adult who cannot speak, use abdominal thrusts; use chest thrusts for late pregnancy or morbid obesity.
If the obstruction persists, continue appropriate clearing efforts during transport. Avoid blind finger sweeps.

cards.title: ASTHMA or COPD WITH WHEEZING / REACTIVE LOWER AIRWAY
pearls: BLS: assist with prescribed inhaler when appropriate; albuterol 2.5 mg by nebulizer per system-specific procedure.
Distinguish BLS from ALS medication choices and reassess respiratory effort during transport.

cards.title: PARTIAL UPPER AIRWAY OBSTRUCTION / EPIGLOTTITIS
pearls: A patient with possible epiglottitis or partial upper-airway obstruction may deteriorate quickly. Minimize agitation and monitor for complete obstruction.
Read the airway and transport directions before intervening; ALS may need advanced airway support.

cards.title: DRUG ASSISTED INTUBATION
pearls: ALS intubation requires ongoing oxygenation, ventilation and confirmation of placement.
This is an advanced airway reference. As an EMT, support BVM, positioning and monitoring under your scope and local direction.

cards.title: CONTINUED SEDATION FOR PATIENTS WITH ADVANCED AIRWAY
pearls: ALS continued sedation is for patients with an advanced airway; review the table for route, dose, monitoring and blood-pressure limits.
The EMT role is to support airway/ventilation and watch for deterioration within scope.

cards.title: ASYSTOLE / PULSELESS ELECTRICAL ACTIVITY (PEA)
pearls: Start high-quality CPR, limit interruptions for rhythm checks, and follow the cardiac-arrest pathway.
Asystole/PEA is nonshockable; ALS medications and reversible-cause assessment are in the full order.

cards.title: BRADYDYSRHYTHMIAS
pearls: Unstable adult bradycardia includes altered mental status with hypoperfusion and SBP under 90.
ALS considers atropine and pacing; do not delay pacing when symptomatic. This is not a BLS medication pathway.

cards.title: CARDIOGENIC SHOCK
pearls: Recognize hypotension and poor perfusion from a cardiac cause; monitor breathing and transport.
ALS considers fluids only in the stated circumstances, rhythm treatment and vasopressors with reassessment.

cards.title: LEFT VENTRICULAR ASSIST DEVICE (LVAD)
pearls: An LVAD patient may have no palpable pulse. Assess perfusion and device function rather than relying on pulse alone.
Bring the controller, batteries and trained caregiver when possible; contact Medical Direction for device or resuscitation questions.

cards.title: NON-TRAUMATIC CARDIAC ARREST (EDWARD EMS ONLY)
pearls: Edward EMS only: follow the system-specific nontraumatic arrest pathway, including mechanical compression device directions.
This order is explicitly restricted to one EMS system in the manual.

cards.title: POLYMORPHIC VENTRICULAR TACHYCARDIA WITH A PULSE
pearls: Polymorphic VT with a pulse may not synchronize reliably; this is an ALS rhythm-management order.
Support perfusion assessment and rapid Medical Direction/ALS involvement.

cards.title: RETURN OF SPONTANEOUS CIRCULATION (ROSC)
pearls: After ROSC, secure airway and ventilation, avoid hyperventilation and monitor for recurrent arrest.
The order describes an EtCO₂ target of 35–45 mmHg and head elevation when blood pressure permits.

cards.title: PULMONARY EDEMA
pearls: For stable pulmonary edema, position upright if SBP is above 100 and assess oxygen needs.
ALS nitroglycerin and CPAP have blood-pressure, mental-status and respiratory criteria; reassess for deterioration.

cards.title: PULSELESS POLYMORPHIC VENTRICULAR TACHYCARDIA
pearls: Pulseless polymorphic VT is a shockable cardiac-arrest rhythm; follow CPR/defibrillation steps and the ALS algorithm.
Do not confuse it with polymorphic VT that retains a pulse.

cards.title: SUPRAVENTRICULAR TACHYCARDIA
pearls: SVT is a narrow-complex rapid rhythm; stability and perfusion guide the ALS pathway.
The order notes vagal maneuvers and warns against adenosine for irregular rapid rhythms.

cards.title: SUSPECTED ACUTE CORONARY SYNDROME (ACS)
pearls: Give aspirin to achieve 324 mg chewed within the last 8 hours unless contraindicated.

BLS prescribed nitroglycerin self-administration is limited to one 0.4 mg sublingual dose when SBP exceeds 140 and there is no contraindication; check PDE-5 inhibitor/riociguat use in the prior 48 hours.
STEMI calls for early Medical Direction contact.

cards.title: VENTRICULAR FIBRILLATION / PULSELESS VENTRICULAR TACHYCARDIA
pearls: Ventricular fibrillation/pulseless VT calls for immediate high-quality CPR and defibrillation as soon as available.
Limit pauses and continue through the full rhythm-specific ALS algorithm.

cards.title: WIDE COMPLEX TACHYCARDIA
pearls: A wide-complex tachycardia with a pulse requires assessment of stability, perfusion and rhythm regularity.
This is an ALS cardioversion/medication decision; support monitoring and transport.

cards.title: INITIAL MEDICAL CARE
pearls: Assess respiratory effort and SpO₂; target 94–98%, or 92% for a patient with COPD history. Assist ventilation with high FiO₂ BVM for inadequate breathing.
Avoid hyperoxia in uncomplicated MI/STEMI, after cardiac arrest, in COPD exacerbation and stroke; assess the patient, not the number alone.

cards.title: ACUTE ABDOMINAL PAIN
pearls: Assess abdominal pain for shock and high-risk causes such as ruptured AAA or ectopic pregnancy.
Start transport early and reassess. ALS pain treatment, antiemetic and fluids depend on perfusion and the full order.

cards.title: ALLERGIC REACTION: NON-ANAPHYLAXIS
pearls: Diffuse hives or wheeze without hypoperfusion is the non-anaphylaxis branch; monitor closely for worsening.
Escalate to anaphylaxis when hypotension, vomiting, severe distress or other systemic deterioration appears.

cards.title: ALLERGIC REACTION: ANAPHYLAXIS
pearls: Recognize multisystem reaction with hypoperfusion, vomiting, altered status or severe breathing trouble.
BLS epinephrine auto-injector 0.3 mg IM is at Medical Control direction under a system-specific protocol; ALS pathways differ for normotension versus shock.

cards.title: BEHAVIORAL EMERGENCIES
pearls: Scene and crew safety come first. Request law enforcement for danger and attempt safe verbal de-escalation.
Consider medical causes of behavior changes, follow restraint policy, and contact Medical Direction for refusal situations described in the order.

cards.title: CHRONIC RENAL FAILURE / DIALYSIS
pearls: Avoid blood pressure and IV attempts in an arm with a dialysis shunt or fistula.
Control fistula bleeding; consider hyperkalemia when the QRS is widened or the patient is unstable.

cards.title: DIABETIC / GLUCOSE EMERGENCIES
pearls: Adult threshold is blood glucose below 60 mg/dL. If alert with intact gag reflex, consider oral glucose.
Protect the airway and reassess; ALS dextrose or glucagon options depend on vascular access.

cards.title: HYPOVOLEMIC SHOCK
pearls: Be alert for significant bleeding and/or amputations. For complete or partial extremity.
Attempt VASCULAR ACCESS IV/IO while transporting.

cards.title: PAIN CONTROL
pearls: Minor pain may be managed with cold packs. The adult ALS analgesia pathway requires attention to severity and SBP.
Once an ALS medication is selected, switching requires Medical Direction approval under this order.

cards.title: SEIZURE / STATUS EPILEPTICUS
pearls: Protect a seizing patient from injury; do not put anything in the mouth. Protect the airway and check glucose.
ALS midazolam route and dose depend on access and weight; review the complete dosing table.

cards.title: SEPSIS
pearls: With known or suspected infection, look for at least two: temperature ≥100.4°F or ≤96.8°F, EtCO₂ ≤25 with square waveform, shock index ≥1, or heart rate >90.
Check glucose and convey a sepsis alert to Medical Direction.

cards.title: STROKE (NON-TRAUMATIC)
pearls: Limit scene time; record last known well, glucose, Cincinnati/FAST findings and VAN per system procedure.
Early Medical Direction contact matters; destination is governed by the separate transport guideline.

cards.title: STROKE TRANSPORT GUIDELINES
pearls: Assess airway and ventilation before considering comprehensive stroke-center bypass.
The order sends patients with last known well 3–4 hours before EMS contact to the closest facility to preserve the treatment window. Use the full VAN/destination chart for other cases.

cards.title: SUSPECTED HYPERKALEMIA
pearls: Suspect hyperkalemia in a renal, crush or metabolic-risk patient with weakness, palpitations, or characteristic ECG changes.
ALS treatment differs for stable versus unstable ECG findings. Obtain and relay ECG information promptly.

cards.title: SYNCOPE / NEAR SYNCOPE
pearls: Syncope can reflect a glucose, cardiac, toxicologic, neurologic or volume problem.
Check glucose, assess for injury and trend vitals; ALS rhythm workup depends on the presentation.

cards.title: BETA BLOCKER OVERDOSE
pearls: Beta-blocker overdose can cause bradycardia and poor perfusion; identify the drug, time and amount, and bring packaging.
BLS supports ABCs and contacts Medical Direction; ALS treatment is in the full order.

cards.title: CALCIUM CHANNEL BLOCKER OVERDOSE
pearls: Calcium-channel blocker overdose can cause bradycardia, hypotension and shock.
Identify the agent and exposure, support ABCs, bring the container and obtain Medical Direction.

cards.title: CARBON MONOXIDE EXPOSURE
pearls: Give high-concentration oxygen or assisted ventilation for suspected carbon monoxide exposure.
Standard pulse oximetry cannot rule out CO poisoning; gather exposure history and consider cyanide in fire victims.

cards.title: CLUB DRUGS
pearls: Suspected club-drug exposure calls for scene safety, ABCs, temperature/mental-status assessment and Medical Direction contact.
Treat complications under the appropriate medical or toxicology order.

cards.title: CYANIDE EXPOSURE
pearls: With fire/smoke exposure and neurologic or cardiovascular collapse, consider cyanide. Use HazMat precautions and support oxygenation.
Hydroxocobalamin is an ALS option under the source order and system availability.

cards.title: CYCLIC ANTIDEPRESSANTS OVERDOSE
pearls: Cyclic antidepressant overdose can produce altered status, seizures, hypotension and conduction disturbance.
Support ABCs and identify the agent; ALS obtains ECG and follows the sodium-bicarbonate pathway.

cards.title: NERVE GAS AUTO-INJECTOR GUIDELINES
pearls: The nerve-agent auto-injector page includes activation and responder-qualification conditions; it is not routine use for an isolated nonspecific symptom.
Follow incident command/decontamination and your EMS system’s authorization and training.

cards.title: OPIOID OVERDOSE
pearls: Prioritize airway and ventilation. BLS naloxone applies when breathing is inadequate or absent, not simply because drug exposure is suspected.
BLS: 2 mg intranasal every 2 minutes, up to 12 mg, until adequate respirations return; contact Medical Direction for additional doses.

cards.title: MUSCARINIC AGENT EXPOSURE
pearls: Muscarinic exposure may cause secretions, bronchospasm, bradycardia and GI symptoms; use HazMat precautions.
Atropine is in the ALS treatment branch. Read the full dose/repeat instructions.

cards.title: SODIUM CHANNEL BLOCKER OVERDOSE
pearls: Suspected sodium-channel blocker toxicity with widened QRS and poor perfusion needs early ALS and ECG assessment.
The ALS branch includes IV fluid and sodium bicarbonate; bring the agent information.

cards.title: COLD EMERGENCIES
pearls: Prevent further heat loss, remove wet clothing, and handle severe hypothermia gently.
In a very cold patient, check a pulse for 30–60 seconds; the order cautions against field confirmation of irreversible death based on appearance.

cards.title: DIVING / SCUBA EMERGENCIES
pearls: Consider decompression illness after diving even when the reported dive seemed safe, including symptoms after later air travel.
Collect dive depth/time/history, support ventilation and consult Medical Direction about hyperbaric destination.

cards.title: FROSTBITE
pearls: Rapidly rewarm frozen areas with tepid water.
Hot packs wrapped in a towel may be used.
DO NOT RUB or massage frozen tissue.

cards.title: HEAT EMERGENCIES
pearls: Move the patient to a cool area and remove excess clothing. Cool the patient and monitor mental status.
Altered mental status raises concern for severe heat illness; do not delay transport.

cards.title: HIGH ALTITUDE EMERGENCIES
pearls: Ask about recent ascent and assess neurologic and respiratory symptoms; high-altitude illness may coexist with trauma.
Support oxygenation and coordinate destination with Medical Direction.

cards.title: SNAKEBITE / ENVENOMATION
pearls: Ensure scene safety and identify the snake if possible without capture or added exposure.
Monitor swelling, perfusion and systemic effects; transport and follow Medical Direction.

cards.title: INITIAL TRAUMA CARE
pearls: Scene safety, airway and spine assessment, ventilation, hemorrhage control, GCS and transport decision come first.
Apply a tourniquet for severe extremity bleeding and document why interventions occur en route.

cards.title: REGION VIII TRAUMA BYPASS CRITERIA
pearls: This page is marked “effective: pending” in the PDF. Check your system’s implementation before relying on it.
It describes an adequate airway and a ≤25-minute transport-time framework for Level I bypass, with specific injury/physiology criteria.

cards.title: TRAUMA TRIAGE AND TRANSPORT GUIDELINES
pearls: For Level I bypass: adequate/patent/secure airway and transport time ≤25 minutes, unless Medical Direction approves an exception.
Use the adult or pediatric injury/physiology criteria and the correct destination order; when an airway cannot be established, transport to closest comprehensive ED.

cards.title: TRAUMATIC CARDIAC ARREST
pearls: In traumatic arrest, scene safety, reversibility and transport priorities differ from a routine medical arrest.
Read the withholding/resuscitation and trauma-specific algorithm before deciding whether to initiate or continue care.

cards.title: MATERNAL TRAUMATIC CARDIAC ARREST
pearls: Maternal traumatic arrest requires coordinated trauma, airway and resuscitation care while transporting.
The order describes leftward uterine displacement/tilt and obstetric assessment where appropriate.

cards.title: REVISED TRAUMA SCORE (RTS)
pearls: The Revised Trauma Score page is a scoring table; calculate its respiratory rate, systolic pressure and GCS components from the source.
Use the score alongside the full triage and transport criteria.

cards.title: SPINE MOTION RESTRICTION (SMR)
pearls: Use the adult SMR decision pathway when a spinal injury is suspected; do not treat a mechanism alone as the entire exam.
The page is largely a diagram; inspect the original chart. Document any crew/patient safety reason the process could not be completed.

cards.title: HEMORRHAGIC SHOCK
pearls: Control external bleeding immediately and check for occult blood loss and shock.
Early transport and ALS vascular access/fluids are guided by perfusion and the source order.

cards.title: HEAD INJURIES
pearls: Begin prompt transport and report findings to Medical Direction. Trend GCS and ventilation.
ALS airway and ventilation steps depend on GCS and signs of herniation.

cards.title: EYE INJURIES
pearls: Check gross visual acuity, discourage straining and avoid pressure on a suspected ruptured globe.
Chemical exposure calls for prompt, copious irrigation without contaminating the uninjured eye; do not irrigate a penetrating globe injury.

cards.title: MORGAN LENS FOR CHEMICAL SPLASH / EYE BURNS (LOYOLA EMS ONLY)
pearls: Loyola EMS only: the Morgan lens chemical-eye pathway is explicitly system restricted.
For other systems, use the eye-injury and chemical-burn orders under your local scope.

cards.title: NECK / SPINE INJURIES
pearls: Apply the indicated SMR and document neurologic deficits, including where sensation changes.
Reassess distal motor/sensory function and transport to the appropriate destination.

cards.title: CHEST / THORACIC INJURIES
pearls: Open chest wounds require a chest seal or occlusive dressing under system procedure; reassess if breathing worsens.
Suspect tension pneumothorax with severe distress and unilateral findings; ALS decompression is a separate step.

cards.title: ABDOMINAL / PELVIC INJURIES
pearls: Begin rapid transport, contact Medical Direction and leave impaled objects in place.
Cover exposed organs with a saline-moistened sterile dressing and an occlusive layer; do not replace them.

cards.title: MUSCULOSKELETAL INJURIES
pearls: Splint injuries and document distal pulse, motor and sensation before and after intervention.
Severe bleeding and amputations need immediate control and careful packaging of amputated tissue.

cards.title: EMD (TASER®) WEAPON INJURIES
pearls: Ensure scene safety and ask law enforcement for baseline behavior and mechanism.
Assess for trauma, altered status and probe locations; address medical causes of agitation.

cards.title: CRUSH INJURIES / ENTRAPMENT
pearls: For significant crush injury, start care during entrapment when safe, identify bleeding, and anticipate deterioration around release.
ALS monitors rhythm and considers fluids and hyperkalemia management under this order.

cards.title: SUSPENSION INJURIES
pearls: Keep the suspended patient’s knees elevated through rescue; do not let the patient stand.
The order specifies positioning during transport and ALS assessment for shock and hyperkalemia.

cards.title: NEAR DROWNING
pearls: After a drowning event, support breathing first, remove wet clothing and prevent further heat loss.
Check temperature and use the cold-emergency or cardiac order as indicated.

cards.title: SUSPECTED ABUSE OR NEGLECT
pearls: Treat injuries and document history, exam, statements and scene findings objectively.
Follow the order’s reporting and destination instructions for suspected domestic, sexual or elder abuse.

cards.title: RADIATION INJURIES
pearls: Follow HazMat command, avoid further contamination and treat the patient’s medical/trauma problems.
Report victim count, status, source and known radiation information to Medical Direction.

cards.title: BLAST INJURIES
pearls: Treat a blast scene as potentially hazardous, including secondary devices, while preserving evidence when possible.
Assess for bleeding, multisystem injury and occult blast-lung injury.

cards.title: BURNS – GENERAL GUIDELINES
pearls: Stop burning, assess airway, remove constricting items, estimate burn size without superficial/first-degree burns and prevent hypothermia.
An unresponsive patient found in a fire merits consideration of cyanide exposure.

cards.title: BURN TRANSPORT GUIDELINES
pearls: A secure airway and transport under 25 minutes are required for direct burn-center bypass under the stated criteria, or obtain direction for an exception.
Criteria include any full-thickness burn, partial-thickness ≥20% TBSA, key areas/joints, inhalation, chemical and certain electrical injuries.

cards.title: RULE OF NINES
pearls: The adult rule-of-nines page is primarily a diagram. Use it to estimate TBSA for the burn pathway.
Exclude superficial burns and compare the diagram with the palm method when appropriate.

cards.title: CHEMICAL BURNS
pearls: Identify the chemical, protect responders, and check whether it reacts with water before irrigation.
Brush off dry powder first, then follow the order’s irrigation and eye-care instructions.

cards.title: ELECTRICAL BURNS
pearls: Before touching the patient, ensure the electrical source is controlled.
Assess entry/exit wounds and neurovascular status; cover with dry sterile dressings. ALS evaluates ECG.

cards.title: INHALATION BURNS
pearls: Hoarseness, stridor, soot, cough and respiratory distress raise concern for inhalation injury.
Support oxygenation/ventilation and notify Medical Direction; soot alone is not a complete airway decision.

cards.title: THERMAL BURNS
pearls: Stop the burn and cover thermal wounds with dry sterile dressings, protecting temperature.
Do not break blisters; follow general-burn and destination rules.

cards.title: MULTIPLE VICTIM INCIDENT (MVI)
pearls: A multiple-victim incident can be managed with available resources under normal procedures.
Reassess resource demand early; escalation to MCI changes triage and coordination.

cards.title: MASS CASUALTY INCIDENT (MCI) / DISASTERS
pearls: An MCI exceeds normal field and receiving-hospital capacity.
Activate the incident/disaster plan and use appropriate triage, resource coordination and destination distribution.

cards.title: START® TRIAGE ALGORITHM
pearls: START is the adult/general MCI triage algorithm; the source page is a flow diagram.
Work through walking ability, respirations, perfusion and mental status in the diagram rather than memorizing a label in isolation.

cards.title: JUMPSTART® TRIAGE ALGORITHM
pearls: JumpSTART adapts MCI triage for pediatric patients; use the source flow diagram.
The pediatric pathway includes a rescue-breathing decision that differs from adult START.

cards.title: SPECIALTY TRANSPORT
pearls: Specialty transport requires Medical Direction coordination and a patient benefit from advanced expertise or destination access.
Review the transport-time, crew and receiving-facility criteria on the source page.

cards.title: EMERGENCY CHILDBIRTH
pearls: If pregnant patient is in cardiac arrest, transport to closest facility regardless of OB capability.
For a pregnant patient with a potentially relevant condition who is not in arrest, choose an appropriate OB/L&D-capable facility; consult Medical Direction if uncertain.

cards.title: APGAR SCORING
pearls: APGAR records appearance, pulse, grimace, activity and respirations.
Use the scoring chart at the appropriate time points while continuing necessary newborn care.

cards.title: DELIVERY COMPLICATIONS – BREECH BIRTH
pearls: Breech delivery is a load-and-go situation; contact Medical Direction promptly.
Support the delivered body without pulling and follow the source’s airway and delivery steps.

cards.title: DELIVERY COMPLICATIONS – SHOULDER DYSTOCIA
pearls: Shoulder dystocia is a load-and-go complication.
The order directs maternal positioning with knees toward shoulders and renewed delivery attempt while contacting Medical Direction.

cards.title: DELIVERY COMPLICATIONS – PROLAPSED CORD
pearls: A prolapsed cord threatens fetal perfusion. Relieve pressure on the cord/presenting part as directed and expedite transport.
Contact Medical Direction and use the complete order for positioning and delivery steps.

cards.title: PREECLAMPSIA
pearls: Preeclampsia may include hypertension and pregnancy-related symptoms; assess mother and fetus and trend vitals.
Position to reduce vena-caval compression and follow the ALS pathway for severe findings.

cards.title: ECLAMPSIA
pearls: Eclampsia adds seizure risk to severe pregnancy-related hypertension.
Protect airway, position appropriately and follow seizure treatment and transport guidance.

cards.title: AIRWAY OBSTRUCTION
pearls: Pediatric airway obstruction: reposition, look for a visible foreign body and use age-appropriate back blows/thrusts.
Assess for anaphylaxis, epiglottitis or tracheostomy/ventilator problems before assuming a foreign body.

cards.title: DRUG ASSISTED INTUBATION
pearls: Pediatric drug-assisted intubation is an ALS procedure for threatened airway or respiratory failure.
EMTs support positioning, BVM ventilation, suction and reassessment under the system’s scope.

cards.title: CONTINUED SEDATION FOR PATIENTS WITH ADVANCED AIRWAY
pearls: Following pediatric advanced-airway placement, ALS sedation and monitoring follow the age/weight-specific table.
Continue ventilation and watch for airway displacement or poor perfusion.

cards.title: REACTIVE LOWER AIRWAY DISEASE / ASTHMA
pearls: BLS may assist with a prescribed beta-agonist MDI.
Assess for retractions, grunting, diminishing sounds and decreasing consciousness; ALS choices and escalation follow the pediatric order.

cards.title: RESPIRATORY ARREST
pearls: In pediatric respiratory arrest, open the airway, ventilate effectively and look for a reversible cause.
Use the age-appropriate cardiac pathway if circulation is lost.

cards.title: RESPIRATORY DISTRESS – HOME VENTILATOR
pearls: For a child on a home ventilator in distress, assess the circuit and consider disconnecting to ventilate with a BVM and high FiO₂.
Caregivers may explain the child’s baseline and equipment; contact Medical Direction and consider ALS backup.

cards.title: RESPIRATORY DISTRESS – TRACHEOSTOMY TUBE
pearls: With a tracheostomy, check for obstruction and suction; remove an inner cannula when indicated.
If ventilation through the tube fails, use the mouth with stoma occluded or ventilate the stoma as directed and confirm chest rise.

cards.title: AED <1 YEAR OF AGE
pearls: If an infant younger than one year is pulseless, start high-quality CPR and apply an AED when available.
Pediatric pads are preferred; the order permits an available AED with attention to pad placement if pediatric equipment is absent.

cards.title: ASYSTOLE / PULSELESS ELECTRICAL ACTIVITY (PEA)
pearls: Pediatric asystole/PEA is a nonshockable arrest pathway.
Start high-quality CPR and ventilation, use the age-appropriate rhythm algorithm and ALS reversible-cause workup.

cards.title: BRADYDYSRHYTHMIAS
pearls: In pediatric bradycardia, oxygenation and ventilation are immediate priorities.
If HR stays below 60 with poor perfusion despite adequate ventilation, follow the CPR/ALS pathway.

cards.title: CARDIOGENIC SHOCK
pearls: Pediatric cardiogenic shock requires careful perfusion and respiratory assessment.
ALS rhythm treatment and any fluid bolus must be balanced against signs of worsening heart failure.

cards.title: NARROW COMPLEX TACHYCARDIA
pearls: Narrow-complex pediatric tachycardia must be assessed for perfusion and stability.
The ALS table separates stable from unstable rhythm management and age/weight dosing.

cards.title: VENTRICULAR FIBRILLATION / PULSELESS VENTRICULAR TACHYCARDIA
pearls: Pediatric VF/pulseless VT calls for immediate CPR and defibrillation with age-appropriate equipment and energy.
Continue ventilation and ALS arrest treatment while limiting rhythm-check pauses.

cards.title: WIDE COMPLEX TACHYCARDIA
pearls: For pediatric wide-complex tachycardia with a pulse, assess stability and perfusion immediately.
ALS synchronized cardioversion or drug treatment depends on the full rhythm chart.

cards.title: INITIAL MEDICAL CARE
pearls: Pediatric means 15 years or younger; distinguish newly born, neonate and infant.
Assess ABCs, respiratory status, glucose when indicated, and use age/weight-specific orders.

cards.title: ALLERGIC REACTION – NON-ANAPHYLAXIS
pearls: Localized pediatric allergic reaction without systemic compromise needs close reassessment for progression.
If shock, vomiting, altered status or severe respiratory findings appear, use the anaphylaxis order.

cards.title: ALLERGIC REACTION – ANAPHYLAXIS
pearls: BLS may consider one epinephrine auto-injector dose: below 30 kg, 0.15 mg; 30 kg or more, 0.3 mg.
This differs from the adult BLS Medical Control wording; refer back to the source and your system-specific scope.

cards.title: BRIEF RESOLVED UNEXPLAINED EVENT (BRUE)
pearls: A BRUE can involve apnea, color change, choking, tone or consciousness change, and the examination may be normal on EMS arrival.
Document caregiver observations and actions, complete pediatric assessment, and transport per the order.

cards.title: DIABETIC / GLUCOSE EMERGENCIES
pearls: The pediatric treatment threshold here is glucose ≤60 mg/dL; compare adult <60 mg/dL.
ALS age-dependent dextrose and glucagon pathways require careful weight and route checks.

cards.title: HYPOVOLEMIC SHOCK
pearls: Control bleeding and assess perfusion in pediatric volume loss or dehydration.
ALS normal saline boluses are 20 mL/kg, reassessed and repeated only as directed in the order.

cards.title: OBSTRUCTIVE SHOCK
pearls: Obstructive shock may result from tension pneumothorax or other blocked cardiac filling/outflow.
Support ABCs and transport; ALS pleural decompression applies when tension pneumothorax is suspected.

cards.title: PAIN CONTROL
pearls: Consider ice packs as needed / appropriate.
Consider NITROUS OXIDE (NITRONOX®) per System-specific procedure.
If pain is severe, and SBP ≥ (70+ (age in years x 2)), consider one of the below. Once.

cards.title: SEIZURES / STATUS EPILEPTICUS
pearls: Clear and protect airway. Vomiting/aspiration precautions.
Protect the patient from injury. Do not place anything in mouth if seizing.
Position patient on side unless contraindicated.

cards.title: SEPSIS
pearls: Known or suspected infection plus two criteria, one of which must be abnormal temperature, prompts consideration of pediatric sepsis.
Use age-specific vital sign thresholds; alert Medical Direction.

cards.title: SYNCOPE / NEAR-SYNCOPE
pearls: Check glucose and consider metabolic, cardiac, volume, toxicologic and neurologic causes of pediatric syncope.
Transport promptly and trend perfusion, rhythm and mental status.

cards.title: BETA BLOCKER OVERDOSE
pearls: Pediatric beta-blocker overdose can cause slow heart rate and shock.
Support ABCs, identify the agent, bring packaging and contact Medical Direction for specific treatment.

cards.title: CALCIUM CHANNEL BLOCKER OVERDOSE
pearls: Pediatric calcium-channel blocker overdose can cause bradycardia and hypoperfusion.
Support ABCs, bring the container and obtain Medical Direction; ALS has a glucagon pathway.

cards.title: CARBON MONOXIDE EXPOSURE
pearls: Give high-concentration oxygen or ventilation in pediatric CO exposure; standard pulse oximetry is unreliable.
Assess all exposed patients and consider cyanide in fire exposure.

cards.title: CLUB DRUGS
pearls: Suspected pediatric club-drug exposure requires scene safety, ABCs, mental-status and temperature evaluation.
Call Medical Direction and treat complications under the appropriate order.

cards.title: CYANIDE EXPOSURE
pearls: Consider cyanide with smoke exposure and rapid neurologic or cardiovascular decline.
Use HazMat precautions, oxygenation and early ALS/Medical Direction; hydroxocobalamin is an ALS option.

cards.title: CYCLIC ANTIDEPRESSANT OVERDOSE
pearls: Pediatric cyclic-antidepressant overdose can cause seizures, shock and conduction delay.
Identify the agent, bring packaging, support ABCs and request ALS/Medical Direction.

cards.title: NERVE GAS AUTO-INJECTOR GUIDELINES
pearls: Pediatric nerve-agent auto-injector treatment follows the incident protocol, decontamination and approved training.
The source page is a dosing/decision chart; use it directly for age-specific details.

cards.title: OPIOID OVERDOSE
pearls: Pediatric suspected opioid overdose: support airway and ventilation. BLS lists one 2 mg intranasal naloxone dose if breathing is inadequate or absent.
Additional BLS doses require Medical Direction; ALS dosing changes at 20 kg.

cards.title: MUSCARINIC AGENT EXPOSURE
pearls: Pediatric muscarinic toxicity causes secretions, breathing difficulty and possibly bradycardia.
Use HazMat precautions and obtain ALS/Medical Direction; atropine dosing is weight dependent.

cards.title: SODIUM CHANNEL BLOCKER OVERDOSE
pearls: Pediatric sodium-channel blocker poisoning can cause a widened QRS and poor perfusion.
Bring the agent container, support ABCs and request ALS; the order includes bicarbonate.

cards.title: COLD EMERGENCIES
pearls: Prevent heat loss and handle a hypothermic child gently.
Assess ventilation and pulse carefully; in arrest, follow the source’s modified defibrillation and rewarming steps.

cards.title: DIVING / SCUBA EMERGENCIES
pearls: Ensure adequate ventilation, HIGH FLOW O2 if indicated.
Contact Medical Direction regarding transport to a hyperbaric chamber.
Keep patient supine or in lateral recovery position.

cards.title: FROSTBITE
pearls: Rapidly rewarm frozen areas with tepid water.
Hot packs wrapped in a towel may be used.
DO NOT RUB or massage frozen tissue.

cards.title: HEAT EMERGENCIES
pearls: Cool a child with suspected heat illness and check for altered mental status or poor perfusion.
Support ABCs and avoid methods that trigger shivering.

cards.title: HIGH ALTITUDE EMERGENCIES
pearls: After ascent, assess pediatric headache, breathing and neurologic complaints while considering trauma.
Support oxygenation and coordinate care with Medical Direction.

cards.title: SNAKEBITE / ENVENOMATION
pearls: Protect the crew, identify exposure without further risk, and assess swelling and perfusion after pediatric envenomation.
Transport, monitor for systemic signs and consult Medical Direction.

cards.title: INITIAL TRAUMA CARE
pearls: Assess and secure scene safety.
Use standard precautions on all patients.
If indicated, follow department HazMat protocols.

cards.title: TRAUMA TRIAGE AND TRANSPORT GUIDELINES
pearls: Pediatric Level I trauma bypass requires airway and ≤25-minute time criteria unless Medical Direction approves an exception.
Use the red/yellow criteria and consider pediatric-capable destinations; inspect the source chart.

cards.title: PEDIATRIC TRAUMA SCORE (PTS)
pearls: The Pediatric Trauma Score combines weight, airway, systolic pressure, consciousness, open wounds and fractures.
Use the source table for scoring and apply transport criteria separately.

cards.title: TRAUMATIC CARDIAC ARREST
pearls: Pediatric traumatic arrest calls for immediate trauma assessment, airway control and transport decisions.
ALS pleural decompression may be considered for the indicated thoracic mechanisms.

cards.title: SPINE MOTION RESTRICTION (SMR)
pearls: In a patient under 9 with suspected neck/spinal cord injury, apply SMR according to this order.
Document safety limits if full SMR cannot be performed.

cards.title: HEMORRHAGIC SHOCK
pearls: Control pediatric hemorrhage and trend perfusion.
ALS uses 20 mL/kg saline boluses with reassessment, to a maximum specified in the order.

cards.title: HEAD INJURIES
pearls: Consider SPINE MOTION RESTRICTION as indicated.
Assess PEDIATRIC GLASGOW COMA SCALE (PGCS).
Treat based on Pediatric GCS.

cards.title: EYE INJURIES
pearls: Quickly assess gross visual acuity in each eye: light perception, motion, acuity.
Discourage patient from sneezing, coughing, straining or bending at the waist.
Elevate head of cot or backboard Semi-Fowler’s position unless contraindicated.

cards.title: NECK / SPINE INJURIES
pearls: Follow pediatric SMR for suspected neck/spine injury and document neurologic findings.
Persistent bradycardia with hypoperfusion has a separate ALS atropine pathway.

cards.title: CHEST / THORACIC INJURIES
pearls: Seal an open chest wound, reassess ventilation and transport promptly.
A suspected tension pneumothorax requires ALS decompression; monitor for worsening after a seal.

cards.title: ABDOMINAL / PELVIC INJURIES
pearls: Initiate rapid transport; contact Medical Direction.
Do not remove impaled objects.
Do NOT attempt to put organs back inside the abdominal cavity.

cards.title: MUSCULOSKELETAL INJURIES
pearls: Control severe bleeding and splint; check distal pulse, movement and sensation.
Wrap amputated tissue in moist gauze inside a sealed bag, then place the bag on ice or cold packs without direct tissue contact.

cards.title: EMD (TASER®) WEAPON INJURIES
pearls: Ensure scene safety and establish the child’s baseline behavior after an EMD/Taser exposure.
Assess probe sites, trauma and altered mental status, and document vitals.

cards.title: CRUSH INJURIES / ENTRAPMENT
pearls: Start care during entrapment when safe, identify bleeding and use a tourniquet when indicated.
Support oxygenation and prepare for reperfusion complications; ALS assesses rhythm and fluids.

cards.title: SUSPENSION INJURIES
pearls: Keep the child’s knees elevated through rescue and do not let the child stand.
Follow the order’s transport position and monitor perfusion after rescue.

cards.title: NEAR DROWNING
pearls: Assess patient's temperature.
If NORMOTHERMIC, treat CARDIAC DYSRHYTHMIAS PER APPROPRIATE SMO.
If HYPOTHERMIC, treat per PEDIATRIC COLD EMERGENCIES SMO.

cards.title: RADIATION INJURIES
pearls: Follow HazMat command and treat the child’s immediate ABC/trauma problems.
Report source and known exposure details to Medical Direction.

cards.title: SUSPECTED CHILD ABUSE / NEGLECT
pearls: Suspected child abuse or neglect requires transport, documentation and reporting to ED staff and DCFS under this order.
Contact Medical Direction if the parent/guardian refuses.

cards.title: BLAST INJURIES
pearls: Look for secondary hazards and multisystem injuries after an explosion.
Control major bleeding, assess airway/lung injury and preserve the scene as directed.

cards.title: BURNS – GENERAL GUIDELINES
pearls: Ensure scene safety, move patient to safe area.
Ensure burning process has stopped.
Consider need for SPINAL MOTION RESTRICTION (SMR).

cards.title: BURN TRANSPORT GUIDELINES
pearls: Age ≤15, secure airway and transport under 25 minutes frame burn-center bypass.
Consider bypass in a burned child below 30 kg even without another listed criterion; consult the complete order for destinations and exceptions.

cards.title: RULE OF NINES
pearls: The pediatric rule-of-nines page is a diagram; compare it with the palm method and exclude superficial injury from TBSA.

cards.title: CHEMICAL BURNS
pearls: HazMat precautions as indicated.
Attempt to obtain name of chemical involved and MSDS/SDS information, if possible.
Certain chemicals will violently react with water, potentially worsening burn injury.

cards.title: ELECTRICAL BURNS
pearls: Ensure the source is safe, assess wounds and neurovascular function, and cover with dry sterile dressings.
ALS evaluates for dysrhythmias and obtains a 12-lead when indicated.

cards.title: INHALATION BURNS
pearls: Inspect for respiratory distress and stridor, support ventilation and notify Medical Direction.
Soot near the airway alone is not an indication for intubation; the order describes when ALS should consider it.

cards.title: THERMAL BURNS
pearls: Stop the burning process, assess airway and burn extent, remove constricting jewelry and protect temperature.
Cover the wound with dry dressings or clean sheets.

cases.prompt: An adult has a regular pulse of 131/min, SBP 118, and no specific complaint. Which ALS-initiation trigger applies?
cases.rationale: The initiation order lists pulse <60 or >130, or irregularity, independent of complaint.

cases.prompt: Which isolated adult SBP meets an ALS-initiation vital-sign trigger in this order?
cases.rationale: Adult trigger is SBP <90 or >200; equality at 90 or 200 does not meet that threshold.

cases.prompt: Once ALS care has begun, who must authorize a downgrade to BLS transport?
options: The patient after signing the PCR
cases.rationale: The initiation-of-ALS order requires online Medical Direction to downgrade or discontinue ALS.

cases.prompt: What is the initial pediatric defibrillation energy in the dosing guide?
cases.rationale: The energy guide gives initial pediatric defibrillation at 2 J/kg, followed by 4 J/kg.

cases.prompt: Which initial pediatric synchronized cardioversion setting appears in the energy guide?
cases.rationale: The dosing guide lists 1 J/kg initial pediatric synchronized cardioversion.

cases.prompt: A conscious late-pregnancy patient is unable to speak or cough after choking. Which maneuver does this adult order use?
cases.rationale: The adult airway obstruction branch substitutes chest thrusts in late pregnancy or morbid obesity.

cases.prompt: The adult wheezing patient already used a prescribed inhaler. Before assisting another use, what should the EMT establish?
options: Last time the inhaler was used
cases.rationale: The BLS branch explicitly calls for determining time of last inhaler use and assisting if appropriate; further doses are at Medical Direction discretion.

cases.prompt: Which nebulized albuterol dose is in the adult BLS wheezing branch, subject to system-specific procedure?
cases.rationale: The adult BLS step lists albuterol 2.5 mg (3 mL) via nebulizer per system-specific procedure.

cases.prompt: Adult severe wheezing persists after epinephrine. Which magnesium regimen is listed?
cases.rationale: The adult reactive lower airway order specifies 2 g in 50–100 mL D5W or NS infused over 10 minutes.

cases.prompt: Adult severe wheezing remains on CPAP and SBP falls to 98 mmHg. What does the order direct first?
cases.rationale: For instability at SBP <100, lower PEEP; remove CPAP if worsening continues.

cases.prompt: Which patient requires Medical Direction contact before IM epinephrine for refractory adult wheezing?
cases.rationale: The order calls for contact when age >50 and/or cardiac disease history.

cases.prompt: In unstable adult bradycardia, what atropine starting dose is specified?
cases.rationale: This June 2024 order lists atropine 0.5 mg rapid IV/IO.

cases.prompt: What is the adult atropine repeat interval and ceiling in this bradycardia order?
cases.rationale: Atropine may repeat every 3–5 minutes up to 3 mg until pacing is available.

cases.prompt: The adult remains hypotensive and bradycardic after atropine. Which initial TCP rate is listed?
cases.rationale: The order starts transcutaneous pacing at 70 beats/min under system procedure.

cases.prompt: Stable pulmonary edema, SBP 139 mmHg: which statement matches the first NTG step?
options: Do not give under the first-dose SBP >140 threshold
cases.rationale: The initial stable pulmonary-edema NTG step requires SBP >140 mmHg.

cases.prompt: After the first NTG dose in stable pulmonary edema, what SBP threshold is used for repeat 0.4 mg SL doses?
cases.rationale: This order uses >140 for the first dose and ≥140 for repeat doses every five minutes.

cases.prompt: CPAP in pulmonary edema requires respiratory distress plus how many additional listed criteria?
cases.rationale: The inclusion box requires respiratory distress and two or more listed findings.

cases.prompt: Pulseless torsades: what initial magnesium dose and route are listed?
cases.rationale: The pulseless polymorphic VT order gives magnesium sulfate 2 g IV/IO diluted in 10 mL NS over two minutes.

cases.prompt: For regular adult SVT, which first two adenosine doses are listed?
cases.rationale: The adult SVT order uses 6 mg then 12 mg rapid IV, each with a 10 mL saline flush.

cases.prompt: An adult tachycardia is narrow-complex but irregular. Which specific medication is cautioned against?
cases.rationale: The SVT order cautions against adenosine for an irregular rapid rhythm.

cases.prompt: Which SBP permits assisting an ACS patient with one prescribed 0.4 mg SL NTG self-dose, assuming no other contraindication?
cases.rationale: The BLS ACS order requires SBP strictly >140 mmHg, prescribed NTG, and no maximum dose or contraindication.

cases.prompt: In the BLS ACS order, which SBP is a reason to withhold assistance with prescribed NTG?
cases.rationale: The June 2024 Region VIII BLS threshold is >140 mmHg; 110 does not qualify.

cases.prompt: A patient took 162 mg aspirin four hours ago. What additional dose reaches the order’s 324 mg total in eight hours?
cases.rationale: The ACS order allows giving aspirin to reach 324 mg total within the last eight hours.

cases.prompt: The patient took 324 mg aspirin seven hours ago. Which aspirin choice follows the ACS order?
cases.rationale: Aspirin may be omitted after ≥324 mg within eight hours, absent another reason for treatment.

cases.prompt: Which recent medication use requires withholding NTG under the ACS order?
cases.rationale: The ACS list includes tadalafil and several PDE-5/pulmonary-hypertension agents within 48 hours.

cases.prompt: For an ALS repeat NTG dose in stable ACS, what additional condition is required?
cases.rationale: The repeat 0.4 mg SL dose after five minutes requires SBP >140 and established IV; the initial dose may precede IV.

cases.prompt: Inferior STEMI leads II, III, aVF: which drug does the ACS special-considerations box say to avoid?
cases.rationale: The order specifically cautions to avoid lidocaine in suspected inferior wall MI.

cases.prompt: Adult VF/pulseless VT: which antiarrhythmic is first-listed when available?
cases.rationale: The order reserves lidocaine for when amiodarone is unavailable; initial amiodarone is 300 mg IV/IO.

cases.prompt: Adult VF remains after initial amiodarone. Which later amiodarone dose appears?
cases.rationale: The later repeat amiodarone dose is 150 mg IV/IO.

cases.prompt: A COPD-history adult is breathing adequately with SpO₂ 89%. Which target is given in initial adult care?
cases.rationale: The adult initial-care oxygen table calls for titration around 92% for COPD/history of COPD.

cases.prompt: Adult non-anaphylactic reaction: what diphenhydramine regimen is listed?
cases.rationale: The non-anaphylaxis order lists diphenhydramine 50 mg slow IV/IO/IM for one dose.

cases.prompt: Adult anaphylaxis: what can BLS give under the system protocol at Medical Control direction?
cases.rationale: The BLS branch specifies one 0.3 mg IM 1:1,000 auto-injector dose at Medical Control direction.

cases.prompt: Anaphylactic shock with IV access: what epinephrine concentration and single-dose increment does this order use?
cases.rationale: The hypotensive/shock ALS branch specifies 1:10,000 epinephrine 0.1 mg slow IV/IO q3 min, max total 0.5 mg.

cases.prompt: Adult anaphylaxis with SBP 94 and perfusion maintained: which ALS epinephrine route applies?
cases.rationale: Normotensive branch (SBP ≥90) specifies 1:1,000, 0.3 mg IM, repeat once after three minutes if needed.

cases.prompt: In adult anaphylaxis, age 52 or cardiac disease history changes which step?
options: Contact Medical Direction before ALS epinephrine
cases.rationale: Both ALS epinephrine branches call for prior Medical Direction contact for age >50 and/or cardiac disease.

cases.prompt: An adult with glucose 60 mg/dL, alert and intact gag: does this order’s oral-glucose threshold apply?
options: Yes, if the patient has a pump
cases.rationale: Adult oral glucose consideration uses glucose strictly below 60 mg/dL.

cases.prompt: An adult with glucose 59 mg/dL is drowsy with no intact gag. What matters for oral glucose?
options: Alertness and intact gag are also required
Only the presence of an insulin pump
cases.rationale: The adult BLS oral-glucose branch requires both alertness and intact gag reflex.

cases.prompt: Adult hypoglycemia with no IV/IO: which fallback medication and dose are listed?
cases.rationale: No-IV/IO branch lists glucagon 1 mg IM once.

cases.prompt: During adult dextrose treatment, how often should blood glucose be reassessed at minimum?
cases.rationale: The adult order states at least every 10 minutes while dextrose is administered.

cases.prompt: Which minimum SBP permits considering the adult moderate/severe pain medication branch?
cases.rationale: The adult pain order uses SBP ≥90 mmHg.

cases.prompt: What is the adult initial fentanyl dose and single-dose ceiling in this order?
cases.rationale: Initial fentanyl is 1 mcg/kg IV/IO/IN, up to 100 mcg.

cases.prompt: If adult fentanyl is chosen for pain, what repeat dose is listed?
cases.rationale: The repeat fentanyl dose is 0.5 mcg/kg IV/IO/IN up to 50 mcg.

cases.prompt: Which pain medication is reserved when fentanyl, ketamine, and morphine are unavailable?
cases.rationale: The adult pain table lists ketorolac only when the other three listed agents are unavailable.

cases.prompt: An actively seizing adult weighs 68 kg. What initial IN/IM midazolam dose appears?
cases.rationale: Adult IN/IM table uses 2.5 mg for weight <70 kg.

cases.prompt: An actively seizing adult weighs exactly 70 kg. What IN/IM midazolam dose appears?
cases.rationale: The adult IN/IM branch uses 5 mg for ≥70 kg.

cases.prompt: What is the adult IV/IO midazolam pattern for active seizure?
options: 2 mg every 2 min to 10 mg total
2 mg every 5 min to 4 mg total
5 mg every 2 min to 20 mg total
cases.rationale: The adult order lists 2 mg IV/IO increments every two minutes to a maximum total of 10 mg.

cases.prompt: Adult suspected infection with HR 110 and SBP 100 has what shock index?
cases.rationale: Shock index is HR ÷ SBP = 110 ÷ 100 = 1.1; ≥1 is one listed adult sepsis criterion.

cases.prompt: Which adult sepsis screening combination can satisfy the two-criterion rule without fever?
cases.rationale: Adult suspected infection requires two listed criteria; HR >90 and shock index ≥1 qualify even without abnormal temperature.

cases.prompt: In adult suspected sepsis, at which SBP does this order call for saline via pressure bag?
cases.rationale: The adult sepsis fluid step is triggered below SBP 120 mmHg.

cases.prompt: Stable suspected hyperkalemia with peaked T waves: which bicarbonate dose is listed?
cases.rationale: The peaked-T branch gives sodium bicarbonate 8.4% 1 mEq/kg IV/IO, up to 50 mEq.

cases.prompt: Unstable suspected hyperkalemia with wide QRS: which nebulized albuterol dose is listed?
cases.rationale: The unstable branch lists albuterol 5 mg (6 mL), may repeat once, with 50 mEq sodium bicarbonate.

cases.prompt: Unstable beta blocker overdose with bradycardic hypoperfusion: which medication is listed?
options: Glucagon 1 mg slow IV, may repeat once
cases.rationale: The beta blocker overdose ALS branch gives glucagon 1 mg slow IV with one repeat permitted.

cases.prompt: Unstable calcium-channel blocker overdose with bradycardic hypoperfusion: what is this edition’s initial listed medication?
cases.rationale: The calcium-channel blocker overdose order lists glucagon 1 mg slow IV, may repeat once.

cases.prompt: Adult cyanide exposure: which hydroxocobalamin regimen is listed?
cases.rationale: The adult cyanide order specifies hydroxocobalamin 5 g over 15 minutes through a dedicated IV line.

cases.prompt: Which IV setup is required for adult hydroxocobalamin?
cases.rationale: The cyanide order requires its own dedicated IV line; no existing IV or piggyback infusion.

cases.prompt: Unstable cyclic-antidepressant overdose with wide QRS: which bicarbonate dose is listed?
cases.rationale: The order gives sodium bicarbonate 8.4% 1 mEq/kg IV/IO, maximum single dose 50 mEq, with saline bolus.

cases.prompt: Adult opioid exposure with adequate breathing: which BLS approach appears before any naloxone trigger?
cases.rationale: When breathing is adequate, place on side and monitor; naloxone is tied to inadequate breathing or apnea.

cases.prompt: Adult apnea after opioid exposure: what BLS intranasal naloxone interval and ceiling are listed?
cases.rationale: The adult BLS order lists 2 mg IN every two minutes, up to 12 mg, while supporting ventilation.

cases.prompt: Which breathing finding meets the opioid order’s definition of inadequate respirations?
cases.rationale: The note defines inadequate as rate <10, EtCO₂ <30, or EtCO₂ >50; exactly 10 does not meet the rate threshold.

cases.prompt: Which EtCO₂ reading alone meets the opioid order’s inadequate-respiration definition?
cases.rationale: The note uses EtCO₂ <30 or >50 mmHg, so 51 meets it while 30 and 50 do not.

cases.prompt: Diphenhydramine overdose with wide QRS and hypoperfusion: which antidysrhythmic therapy is listed?
cases.rationale: The sodium-channel blocker order lists 1 mEq/kg sodium bicarbonate IV/IO, max single 50 mEq, plus saline.

cases.prompt: A severely hypothermic adult appears pulseless. How long does the cold-emergency order allow for a pulse check?
cases.rationale: The hypothermia order allows a 30–60-second pulse check before deciding there is no pulse.

cases.prompt: Adult heat emergency with glucose 59 mg/dL: which parallel protocol becomes relevant?
cases.rationale: The heat order directs treatment under adult diabetic/glucose emergencies when glucose is <60 mg/dL.

cases.prompt: After a snakebite, transport exceeds what duration before specialty transport should be considered?
cases.rationale: Adult snakebite order says consider specialty transport when transport time >15 minutes.

cases.prompt: A red-criteria trauma patient has an adequate airway; Level I travel is 26 minutes. What does the bypass time rule say absent approval?
options: Wait for a helicopter regardless of time
cases.rationale: Region VIII trauma bypass generally limits Level I travel to 25 minutes without Medical Direction approval.

cases.prompt: A trauma patient meets Level I criteria but the airway cannot be adequately maintained. What destination instruction takes precedence?
options: Remain on scene for a full assessment
cases.rationale: The transport order directs the closest comprehensive ED when an adequate airway cannot be established/maintained.

cases.prompt: Adult hemorrhagic shock without signs of head injury: which SBP is the fluid target?
cases.rationale: The adult hemorrhagic shock order targets SBP 90 mmHg; suspected head injury changes the target to 110.

cases.prompt: Adult hemorrhagic shock with suspected head injury: which SBP target replaces the usual trauma target?
cases.rationale: The order raises the fluid target to SBP 110 mmHg when head-injury signs are present.

cases.prompt: Severe adult head injury with herniation signs: what EtCO₂ target is in the order?
cases.rationale: The head-injury order uses a target EtCO₂ around 30 mmHg when signs of herniation are present.

cases.prompt: After sealing an open chest wound, ventilation deteriorates. What action is specified?
options: Lift/remove the dressing briefly to release trapped air
Add a second fully occlusive layer
cases.rationale: The adult thoracic injury order calls for lifting/removing the dressing if the patient worsens.

cases.prompt: Which care for abdominal evisceration follows the adult order?
options: Saline-moistened sterile dressing and occlusive covering without replacement
Firm direct pressure directly on exposed bowel
cases.rationale: The order calls for saline-moistened sterile dressing and occlusive layer; do not replace organs.

cases.prompt: Adult burns requiring fluid resuscitation: what starting saline rate is listed?
cases.rationale: The adult general burns order lists normal saline at 500 mL/hr for fluid resuscitation.

cases.prompt: What is the adult burn-center direct-transport time limit, absent Medical Direction exception?
cases.rationale: The adult burn transport guideline uses <25 minutes to a burn center under its criteria.

cases.prompt: Chemical skin burn without water-reactive concern: what irrigation goal is specified?
cases.rationale: The chemical-burn order calls for copious irrigation for a goal of at least 30 minutes, continued during transport.

cases.prompt: A fresh thermal burn occurred 10 minutes ago. For how long at most should the area be cooled?
cases.rationale: The adult thermal-burn order limits cooling to five minutes if the injury occurred within 15 minutes.

cases.prompt: An adult MCI patient starts breathing after airway repositioning. Which triage framework is used?
cases.rationale: The adult MCI diagram is START; pediatric patients use JumpSTART.

cases.prompt: A child remains apneic after opening the airway in MCI triage. What pediatric-specific step follows?
cases.rationale: JumpSTART includes rescue breathing before the final apnea determination.

cases.prompt: After delivery, what interval is given for expected placenta delivery?
cases.rationale: The postpartum childbirth phase says the placenta should deliver in 20–30 minutes.

cases.prompt: What estimated postpartum blood-loss threshold activates the hemorrhage actions in the childbirth order?
cases.rationale: The postpartum phase calls out estimated blood loss >500 mL.

cases.prompt: Preeclampsia with qualifying severe findings: what magnesium regimen is listed?
cases.rationale: The preeclampsia order gives magnesium sulfate 2 g in 50–100 mL D5W/NS over ten minutes.

cases.prompt: Eclampsia: what magnesium regimen distinguishes it from the preeclampsia infusion?
options: 2 g IV/IO over 2 min, may repeat once
cases.rationale: The eclampsia order gives 2 g IV/IO over two minutes, may repeat once to 4 g total.

cases.prompt: A 28-kg child remains in severe asthma distress. What epinephrine IM dose is in the pediatric order?
cases.rationale: Pediatric reactive lower airway order uses 0.15 mg IM for <30 kg and 0.3 mg for ≥30 kg.

cases.prompt: What is the maximum pediatric magnesium sulfate dose for severe reactive lower airway disease?
cases.rationale: The pediatric asthma order uses 25 mg/kg IV/IO over ten minutes with a maximum of 2 g.

cases.prompt: A child in respiratory arrest has HR 55/min after effective ventilation. Which order should you enter?
options: Pediatric opioid overdose regardless of exposure
cases.rationale: The pediatric respiratory-arrest order directs bradydysrhythmias when HR <60.

cases.prompt: For a pulseless infant under one year, only an adult AED is available. Which approach matches the SMO?
options: Use AED with pads arranged not to overlap
Withhold all AED use under age one
Use AED only after five rounds of CPR
cases.rationale: Pediatric capability is preferred, but the order allows an AED with careful non-overlapping pad placement.

cases.prompt: A child remains at HR 58/min with hypoperfusion after effective oxygenation and ventilation. What action is indicated?
cases.rationale: The pediatric bradycardia order starts CPR when HR remains <60 with hypoperfusion despite adequate ventilation.

cases.prompt: Pediatric atropine for vagal/primary AV block: what IV/IO dose is listed?
cases.rationale: The pediatric bradycardia order lists atropine 0.02 mg/kg IV/IO.

cases.prompt: What is the pediatric atropine minimum single dose?
cases.rationale: The atropine box gives a 0.1 mg minimum, 0.5 mg max single dose.

cases.prompt: For pediatric cardiopulmonary compromise, which epinephrine IV/IO dose is listed?
cases.rationale: Pediatric bradycardia lists 1:10,000 epinephrine 0.01 mg/kg (0.1 mL/kg) IV/IO.

cases.prompt: Pediatric narrow-complex tachycardia: a 10-month-old has HR 221/min. Which age-specific rate threshold is crossed?
cases.rationale: The pediatric order uses >220/min under age one and >180/min for ages one through 15.

cases.prompt: What is the first pediatric adenosine dose for narrow-complex tachycardia?
cases.rationale: The first dose is 0.1 mg/kg rapid IV/IO, maximum 6 mg, followed by saline flush.

cases.prompt: What is the pediatric second adenosine dose and maximum?
cases.rationale: The next pediatric adenosine dose is 0.2 mg/kg, maximum 12 mg.

cases.prompt: Pediatric VF/pulseless VT: which shock sequence appears?
cases.rationale: The pediatric VF/VT order begins at 2 J/kg, then 4 J/kg.

cases.prompt: Pediatric VF/pulseless VT: what amiodarone dose is listed?
cases.rationale: The order lists amiodarone 5 mg/kg IV/IO for shockable pulseless arrest, up to three doses.

cases.prompt: Pediatric wide-complex tachycardia with pulse: which initial synchronized cardioversion energy is listed?
cases.rationale: The pediatric wide-complex tachycardia order uses 1 J/kg initially.

cases.prompt: A patient is exactly 15 years old. Which initial-care pathway applies in this edition unless an order specifies otherwise?
cases.rationale: The pediatric initial medical care order includes patients through age 15.

cases.prompt: Pediatric nausea treatment at 39 kg: which ondansetron option is listed?
cases.rationale: Under 40 kg, pediatric initial care lists 2 mg slow IV once with no repeat dose.

cases.prompt: Pediatric nausea treatment at exactly 40 kg: which ondansetron option is listed?
options: 4 mg slow IV or 4 mg ODT once
cases.rationale: At ≥40 kg, the order lists 4 mg slow IV or 4 mg ODT once, no repeat.

cases.prompt: Pediatric non-anaphylactic allergy: what diphenhydramine dose and ceiling are listed?
cases.rationale: The pediatric order uses diphenhydramine 1 mg/kg IM or slow IV, maximum 50 mg.

cases.prompt: Pediatric anaphylaxis at 29 kg: what auto-injector dose is listed?
cases.rationale: Pediatric BLS auto-injector dose is 0.15 mg below 30 kg.

cases.prompt: Pediatric anaphylaxis at exactly 30 kg: what auto-injector dose is listed?
cases.rationale: Pediatric BLS auto-injector dose is 0.3 mg at ≥30 kg.

cases.prompt: Pediatric anaphylaxis with IV/IO: what saline bolus is first listed?
